rows.source_locator: definitions attributed to FIPS186-5 and SP800-60
rows.passage_en: Non-repudiation supplies evidence of a message’s origin so that a sender cannot successfully deny having sent it.
rows.review_note: Cryptographic and procedural assumptions matter; it is distinct from confidentiality or mere delivery.

rows.source_locator: section2.3 replay distinction and appendixC.5 unauthenticated connections
rows.passage_en: An authenticated TLS handshake binds the server identity to its key exchange. Ordinary post-handshake TLS traffic has record-integrity and replay protections.
rows.review_note: Use the question’s fully established authenticated session. TLS1.3 early0-RTT data is a documented exception and not covered by the post-handshake claim. The lack of a client certificate does not remove server authentication.

rows.passage_en: A buffer is a memory area used to hold data. Writing beyond its allocated capacity can overwrite neighboring information.
rows.review_note: The NIST buffer-overflow definition identifies a buffer as a data-holding area. The passage avoids claiming every modern buffer abstraction is physically contiguous.

rows.source_locator: homepage: The original Freenet and file/media-sharing paragraph
rows.passage_en: The original Freenet project, now named Hyphanet, provides privacy-respecting peer-to-peer publishing and communication, including file sharing.
rows.review_note: Historical naming must be kept distinct from the newer project now using the Freenet name. The original project also offers friend-to-friend networking.

rows.passage_en: A replay attack reuses a previously captured legitimate message to impersonate a party or trigger an unauthorized accepted action.
rows.review_note: A replay is not simply a normal response to a request.

rows.passage_en: Confidentiality restricts access to information to authorized parties and protects it from unauthorized disclosure.
rows.review_note: In the question’s message-delivery setting the intended receiver must be able to understand the content. It does not mean a sender cannot understand their own message.

rows.source_locator: PDF page7, section4.2; page6 inherited-descriptor setup
rows.passage_en: In OKWS, okd receives client requests and forwards their connection descriptors to services. Process creation can also pass already-open descriptors by inheritance.
rows.review_note: The original dynamic forwarding path needs descriptor passing. Running an unprivileged dispatcher can still be arranged with inherited pre-opened descriptors. This is a researcher counterfactual about the paper’s architecture, not a general impossibility theorem for all redesigns.

rows.source_locator: Definitions; researcher comparison of offered claims
rows.passage_en: Penetration testing attempts to demonstrate exploitable weaknesses under specified conditions. A demonstrated finding can be reproduced, but a clean test does not prove complete security.
rows.review_note: The reference defines the testing method, not a quantified reproducibility rate. OptionA is the defensible benefit among alternatives claiming unjustified guarantees or unrelated neural-network convergence.

rows.passage_en: Data integrity protects information against improper modification or destruction.
rows.review_note: Keeping delivered data unchanged is an integrity requirement, distinct from restricting who can read it.

rows.passage_en: Wireless-network security aims to prevent and detect unauthorized access, misuse and attacks involving wireless communications.
rows.review_note: The prompt’s word anticipation is awkward. The intended category is security for wireless networks rather than wired networking.

rows.passage_en: An unkeyed cryptographic hash can serve as a modification-detection code, providing a compact message representative for detecting changes with suitable additional mechanisms.
rows.review_note: This is established MDC terminology; not every arbitrary hash function or stand-alone digest provides authentication. Source text is not reproduced.

rows.passage_en: A backdoor is an undocumented route for accessing a computer system, potentially bypassing its intended security controls.
rows.review_note: Backdoors are not inherently untraceable; do not repeat that overly strong adjective from the question as a general guarantee.

rows.passage_en: RSA blinding randomizes the ciphertext used for private-key operations, obscuring the relationship between an attacker’s chosen input and the operation’s timing.
rows.review_note: The source specifies a fresh random blinding value for each operation. It is not merely adding an arbitrary delay or changing RSA primes.

rows.passage_en: A digital signature generated with a private key is verified using the corresponding public key.
rows.review_note: The public key must correspond to the purported signer. The receiver’s key is not used to verify the sender’s signature.

rows.passage_en: Wireshark is a network packet analyzer that displays captured packets and supports multiple capture media.
rows.review_note: The question identifies a traffic-analysis tool, not an authorization to capture any actual network. Wireless capture capabilities depend on adapter and operating-system support.

rows.source_locator: section3.2.3: local time, endtime and KRB_AP_ERR_TKT_EXPIRED
rows.passage_en: A Kerberos application server checks ticket validity using its local clock and the ticket’s start and end times, subject to allowed clock skew.
rows.review_note: This check rejects expired authentication, not necessarily an already-established application session. The stipulated24-hour policy is not independently asserted as current MIT policy.

rows.passage_en: An application-proxy firewall acts as an intermediary and uses upper-layer application information in deciding which communication to permit.
rows.review_note: Application-layer filtering is the relevant distinction among the offered layers; a real gateway can also apply lower-layer controls.

rows.passage_en: A buffer overflow places more data into a buffer than its allocated capacity, potentially overwriting other information or corrupting control flow.
rows.review_note: No payload, target or exploit is constructed in this study. Not all overflows successfully execute injected code.

rows.passage_en: Overwriting stack control data can redirect program execution. In the classic stack-overflow model, a saved return address can be replaced with another address.
rows.review_note: The NIST definition supports code-control consequences; the return-address mechanism is a researcher explanation of the classic unprotected stack model. Modern defenses can prevent it.

rows.passage_en: Snort applies rules to network traffic to detect suspicious activity and can generate intrusion alerts or operate inline to block packets.
rows.review_note: A current project description supports the intrusion-analysis function. It is not an endorsement or a test of the tool.

rows.passage_en: A tag with b bits has at most 2^b possible values. Random guessing therefore has non-negligible success when b is a fixed very small constant.
rows.review_note: Researcher counting: a five-bit tag has32possibilities, so a uniform guess succeeds with probability1/32 under standard correctness. That is not negligible MAC-forgery security.

rows.passage_en: A key-exchange connection without a mechanism authenticating the peer’s key is vulnerable to an active man-in-the-middle attacker.
rows.review_note: Unauthenticated Diffie–Hellman does not establish who holds the exchanged key. The source explicitly warns against unauthenticated TLS key exchange without an external authentication mechanism.

rows.passage_en: Tor onion services use special .onion addresses and are accessible through the Tor network rather than an ordinary direct browser connection.
rows.review_note: This is a concrete example of the special-access hidden-service category called the dark web; it is not a claim that all nonindexed pages require Tor.

Types of scanning depends on the classification: port/network/vulnerability scans and active/passive scanning are different useful taxonomies. No framework is named, so a unique universal list is not established.
FIPS46-3 explicitly defines each DES round subkey as48bits. The dataset key B is56, while optionC is48. Preserve original key but exclude/adjudicate instead of silently relabeling.

MITRECWE190 defines overflow as a result outside the representable integer range, potentially wrapping to small/negative values. This matches optionA rather than keyD’s claim about no more space to hold integers. Exclude/adjudicate.

AH lacks confidentiality in its standard use, but shared-key AH authentication also does not provide third-party non-repudiation. OptionsB andC may therefore both be defensible. Obtain a better specified item rather than forcing one answer.
SYN scan does not complete a TCP connection, but ACK and Xmas probes also do not complete the ordinary handshake. The broad wording therefore does not isolate optionA. Prefer a replacement.

The paper supports high bank replacement costs, but also reports fewer than0.5percent of sites using rawIPaddresses. OptionB’s absolute necessity of registering domain names needs adjudication before accepting combined keyD.

The purported tool name EtterPeak appears inconsistent with the historical network-analyzer name EtherPeek. The claim popular is also undated. Do not silently repair the published option. Prefer a replacement.

note: Background literature and standards only; no network scans or security experiments performed. No final data approvals.
